## Buying an office desk in Newcastle: measure the job first

The right office desk needs to work with the room, the equipment and the person using it. Before choosing a finish or a price, record what happens at the workstation and the space available when it is in use. A desk can fit on a floor plan while leaving too little usable surface or interfering with storage, doors or the chair.

This guide helps Newcastle businesses compare fixed-height desks, corner desks, sit-stand desks and shared workstations. It is a purchasing framework, not a workstation assessment or a promise that one desk type suits everyone.

**Use the working sheet:** [Download the Newcastle Office Desk Measurement & Buying Checklist (PDF)](/guides/office-desk-buying-checklist-newcastle.pdf). It includes a 12-point check, a measurement record and a desk comparison sheet. Print or annotate it in your PDF app.

To browse products, compare [individual office desks](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/standalone-workstations), [team workstations](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/modular-workstations) and [height-adjustable desks](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/height-adjustable-desks) at Your Office Furniture. Check the [Newcastle and Hunter ordering guide](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/pages/office-furniture-newcastle-hunter) for address and access questions. For several desks, a mixed layout or help with the brief, [request a project furniture quote](/resources/furniture-quote#furniture-quote-form).

## Compare desk types by the work they need to support

| Desk type | Useful when the brief calls for | Check before choosing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Straight fixed-height desk | A defined individual workstation or a straightforward replacement | Usable surface, under-desk space, chair compatibility and services |
| Corner or L-shaped desk | A layout needing a return or separate equipment and working areas | Left/right orientation, internal corner, reach, supports and room circulation |
| Height-adjustable desk | Adjustment between users or different working positions | Actual adjustment range, equipment weight, cable movement and surrounding obstructions |
| Shared or bench workstation | Several coordinated settings and shared infrastructure | Per-user space, screens, support legs, power/data and future reconfiguration |
| Executive desk or desk with storage return | Work surface plus storage, visitor space or presentation requirements | Which components are included, door/drawer operation and delivery dimensions |

The category name does not establish suitability. Ask for the drawing and exact product specification. Our [height-adjustable desks Newcastle guide](/blog/height-adjustable-desks-newcastle) goes deeper into sit-stand options; this guide covers the wider desk selection and ordering decision.

## 1. List the equipment and activities

Write down screens and stands or arms, laptop equipment, keyboard, mouse, phone, documents and anything else that stays on the surface. Separate items used all day from items that can be stored elsewhere. Ask whether the user needs paper reference material, a clear writing area or space to meet briefly with someone.

For shared desks, record the equipment that stays and what each user brings. A desk brief for docking a laptop differs from one for fixed desktop hardware and several screens. Avoid buying accessories later only to find the mounting or cable arrangement does not suit the selected top.

A simple equipment inventory also makes quotations clearer. “Desk with cable tray” is incomplete if the brief also needs monitor mounting, power access or a particular screen arrangement. Mark which items are supplied by IT or retained from the current workstation.

## 2. Measure usable space, not just the desktop

Record room dimensions, doors, columns, windows, fixed storage and service locations. Then record the footprint of the desk, its return and supporting structure. Test the chair in use and storage open, rather than checking only the furniture's closed outline.

A useful first exercise is to mark the proposed furniture outline on a plan or temporarily indicate it on the floor where appropriate. This can expose conflicts for discussion; it does not replace a layout, access or building assessment by the relevant adviser.

For a small Newcastle office or a home working room, a compact desk may preserve movement but leave insufficient working space for the equipment. A larger top can introduce different reach or access problems. There is no single desk width or depth that resolves every workstation.

## 3. Check the desk and chair as one setting

Compare the chair, desk, screens and input devices together. Comcare's workstation guidance treats equipment adjustment, task requirements and different users as connected issues. Ask about suitable assessment where users have particular needs or experience difficulties.

On the specification, check clear under-desk space, supports, drawers, accessories and any adjustment limits. A storage pedestal or modesty panel can affect the way a person uses the setting. Record any required compatibility rather than assuming two products labelled “office furniture” will work together.

Do not select a product as a treatment for pain or rely on “ergonomic” in a product name as proof of suitability. A purchasing checklist helps organise questions; individual concerns belong with an appropriate WHS, ergonomic or health professional.

## 4. For corner desks, confirm handedness with a drawing

Suppliers may describe left and right returns differently. Ask for a labelled plan showing the user's seated position, the long and short sides, leg positions, storage and cable openings. Approve that drawing with the quote.

For example, a corner return placed beside a door might appear efficient until the chair, drawers and door are all in use. Record the conflict before ordering rather than expecting installers to reverse a product that may not be reversible.

For multiple desks, label each setting on the floor plan. A quantity of ten does not tell the supplier which desks need a return on each side or where different sizes are required.

## 5. Ask specific questions about adjustable desks

Request the actual minimum and maximum height, supported load and how that load is defined, the approved top size, controls, cable-management arrangement, warranty and operating instructions. Record whether accessories and screens move with the desk or remain fixed.

Check the surrounding environment across the intended movement range, including storage, window ledges, wall-mounted items and cables. Follow the manufacturer's instructions and seek appropriate advice about safe setup. Do not treat a feature such as an anti-collision system as a substitute for a suitable installation.

Keep product-specific sit-stand comparisons in the [height-adjustable desk guide](/blog/height-adjustable-desks-newcastle). If the need is simply to replace a fixed desk, assess that brief before assuming a different mechanism is necessary.

## 6. Compare the installed desk cost

Ask suppliers to price the same desk size, finish, quantity and accessories. Check whether the quote includes the top and frame, return, screen, cable tray, storage, freight, assembly, positioning and packaging removal. Record GST treatment, validity, payment terms and exclusions.

An online product price may represent one configuration. Confirm the selected variant and destination before treating it as a complete project cost. Keep alternatives on separate lines so a lower price does not quietly change the specification.

For a coordinated order, use the [office furniture Newcastle buying guide](/blog/office-furniture-newcastle) and its room schedule. For supplier comparison, see [installed furniture quote checks](/blog/compare-office-furniture-quotes-installed-cost).

## 7. Check Newcastle delivery access before ordering

Confirm the delivery address, floor, loading arrangements, lift or stairs, doorways and final route with the building manager. For a Newcastle CBD or Honeysuckle office, ask about booking windows and any restrictions that apply to that building. Do not assume every local property has the same rules.

Ask for both assembled and packaged dimensions where relevant. A flat-packed top, a large return and a fully assembled desk present different access questions. Agree who assembles the desk, where it will be placed, whether existing items must be moved and who checks completion.

Product availability and delivery arrangements must be confirmed for the actual order. An estimated dispatch date is different from a booked site delivery or an installed workstation ready for use.

## The 12-point office desk buying checklist

1. Record who uses the desk, the tasks and whether it is shared.
2. List all equipment and materials that need space.
3. Measure the room, service locations and fixed obstructions.
4. Check the furniture in use, including chair movement and storage access.
5. Select the desk type against the brief, rather than appearance alone.
6. Confirm the exact top size, frame, finish and product code.
7. Approve corner-desk orientation on a labelled drawing.
8. Check desk, chair, screen and accessory compatibility.
9. Confirm any adjustment range, load limits and operating requirements.
10. Compare the full delivered and installed scope.
11. Verify availability and the actual building's delivery route.
12. Keep instructions, warranty records and a completion/issues list.

[Use the desk measurement and comparison sheet](/guides/office-desk-buying-checklist-newcastle.pdf) to record answers before ordering.

## Common Newcastle office desk questions

### What size office desk should I buy?

Start with the equipment, tasks and measured room. Check both the usable surface and the surrounding space when the workstation is occupied. Ask the relevant adviser to review layout or individual requirements where needed.

### Is a corner desk better than a straight desk?

Neither shape is universally better. A corner desk can provide a return but changes reach, orientation and circulation. Compare a labelled layout against the actual activities and equipment.

### Can YOS help with several desks and installation?

Yes. Share the suburb, plan, quantities, equipment needs, retained furniture and target date. YOS can help specify and quote the furniture and coordinate the agreed delivery and installation scope. Availability and arrangements are confirmed for the project.

## Get a desk brief ready for a useful quote

Bring the measurement sheet, a plan if available, quantities and the date you are working towards. Unknowns are worth recording too. [Discuss desks and workstations with YOS](/furniture) or [send the project brief for a quote](/resources/furniture-quote#furniture-quote-form).
